<!-- BEGIN EMBEDDED MARKDOWN -->
<script type="text/plain" id="markdown-source"># Document Loader Comparison

This repository compares [Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling), [Unstructured](https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured), and [Marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker) as small, independent document-to-Markdown batch pipelines. Each loader has its own Python environment because the pinned dependency sets are incompatible.

## Docling 2.113.0

### Conversion approach

Docling parses an input into its structured document model, including detected layout and document objects, and then serializes that model with `export_to_markdown()`.

### Strengths

- Produces Markdown from a unified structural representation rather than from a local element-by-element formatter.
- Supports the repository's mixed source discovery while applying an explicit PDF backend for PDF inputs.
- Keeps conversion and Markdown export behind a compact API.

### Tradeoffs

- Document analysis and model initialization can be resource-intensive, especially on a first run.
- A written output does not by itself prove every page was processed completely; page-level preprocessing failures require separate validation.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-docling\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\docling_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/`, creates one `DocumentConverter`, and configures PDFs with `PyPdfiumDocumentBackend`.
- For each file it calls `converter.convert()`, exports `result.document` to Markdown, and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `docling_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Unstructured 0.24.1

### Conversion approach

Unstructured's automatic `partition()` function turns each document into typed elements. The repository then uses its own `elements_to_markdown()` adapter: `Title` becomes a level-one heading, `Header` a level-two heading, `ListItem` a bullet, and every other category a plain paragraph.

### Strengths

- Typed elements make the intermediate result easy to inspect or process differently downstream.
- Automatic partitioning provides a broad-format entry point.
- The local Markdown mapping is short, explicit, and easy to adjust.

### Tradeoffs

- The lightweight adapter discards most element metadata and does not preserve all layout or hierarchy available from Unstructured.
- Categories outside the three special cases are flattened to plain paragraphs, so complex structures can lose fidelity.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-unstructured\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\unstructured_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/` and calls `partition(filename=...)` separately for each one.
- It converts the returned elements with `elements_to_markdown()` and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `unstructured_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Marker 1.10.2

### Conversion approach

Marker uses a model-backed, PDF-oriented `PdfConverter`. The repository creates the converter from `create_model_dict()`, renders each source, and extracts the Markdown string with `text_from_rendered()`.

### Strengths

- Targets structured Markdown recovery from PDFs, including layout-heavy content.
- Uses a single rendered result from which the repository directly extracts Markdown.
- Can benefit substantially from CUDA acceleration on complex documents.

### Tradeoffs

- It is the most PDF-specific path; unsupported source formats fail per file.
- Model loading and conversion are computationally heavy, particularly with CPU-only PyTorch.
- The default configuration can retain running headers, produce broken image references or mojibake, and encounter worker or deeply nested rendering failures on difficult PDFs.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-marker\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\marker_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/`, initializes one `PdfConverter` with default Marker 1.10.2 configuration, and processes files sequentially.
- For each file it calls the converter, takes the first value returned by `text_from_rendered()`, and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `marker_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Choosing a loader

- Choose Docling when a structured document model and direct Markdown export are the best fit.
- Choose Unstructured when typed elements and a customizable local mapping are more useful than high-fidelity Markdown serialization.
- Choose Marker when PDF-focused, model-backed structure recovery justifies the greater compute cost and narrower input support.

All three runners overwrite an existing output for the same source-relative path. They are comparison scripts rather than a shared production ingestion pipeline, and generated Markdown should be evaluated for reading order, headings, lists, tables, equations, images, and metadata instead of by file size alone.
</script>

  <script>
    (() => {
      "use strict";

      const source = document.getElementById("markdown-source").textContent;
      const target = document.getElementById("document");

      const escapeHtml = (value) => value
        .replaceAll("&", "&amp;")
        .replaceAll("<", "&lt;")
        .replaceAll(">", "&gt;")
        .replaceAll('"', "&quot;")
        .replaceAll("'", "&#39;");

      const renderInline = (value) => {
        const code = [];
        let html = value.replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, (_, contents) => {
          code.push(`<code>${escapeHtml(contents)}</code>`);
          return `\u0000CODE${code.length - 1}\u0000`;
        });

        html = escapeHtml(html).replace(
          /\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)/g,
          (_, label, href) => {
            const safeHref = /^(https?:\/\/|\.\.?\/|#)/.test(href) ? href : "#";
            return `<a href="${escapeHtml(safeHref)}">${label}</a>`;
          }
        );

        return html.replace(/\u0000CODE(\d+)\u0000/g, (_, index) => code[Number(index)]);
      };

      const renderMarkdown = (markdown) => {
        const lines = markdown.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n").split("\n");
        const output = [];
        let paragraph = [];
        let inList = false;

        const closeParagraph = () => {
          if (paragraph.length) output.push(`<p>${renderInline(paragraph.join(" "))}</p>`);
          paragraph = [];
        };
        const closeList = () => {
          if (inList) output.push("</ul>");
          inList = false;
        };

        for (const line of lines) {
          const heading = /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/.exec(line);
          const item = /^-\s+(.+)$/.exec(line);

          if (heading) {
            closeParagraph();
            closeList();
            const level = heading[1].length;
            output.push(`<h${level}>${renderInline(heading[2])}</h${level}>`);
          } else if (item) {
            closeParagraph();
            if (!inList) {
              output.push("<ul>");
              inList = true;
            }
            output.push(`<li>${renderInline(item[1])}</li>`);
          } else if (!line.trim()) {
            closeParagraph();
            closeList();
          } else {
            closeList();
            paragraph.push(line.trim());
          }
        }

        closeParagraph();
        closeList();
        return output.join("\n");
      };

      try {
        target.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(source);
      } catch (error) {
        target.innerHTML = '<p id="render-error">The embedded document could not be rendered.</p>';
        console.error(error);
      }
    })();
  </script>

# Document Loader Comparison

This repository compares [Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling), [Unstructured](https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured), and [Marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker) as small, independent document-to-Markdown batch pipelines. Each loader has its own Python environment because the pinned dependency sets are incompatible.

## Docling 2.113.0

### Conversion approach

Docling parses an input into its structured document model, including detected layout and document objects, and then serializes that model with `export_to_markdown()`.

### Strengths

- Produces Markdown from a unified structural representation rather than from a local element-by-element formatter.
- Supports the repository's mixed source discovery while applying an explicit PDF backend for PDF inputs.
- Keeps conversion and Markdown export behind a compact API.

### Tradeoffs

- Document analysis and model initialization can be resource-intensive, especially on a first run.
- A written output does not by itself prove every page was processed completely; page-level preprocessing failures require separate validation.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-docling\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\docling_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/`, creates one `DocumentConverter`, and configures PDFs with `PyPdfiumDocumentBackend`.
- For each file it calls `converter.convert()`, exports `result.document` to Markdown, and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `docling_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Unstructured 0.24.1

### Conversion approach

Unstructured's automatic `partition()` function turns each document into typed elements. The repository then uses its own `elements_to_markdown()` adapter: `Title` becomes a level-one heading, `Header` a level-two heading, `ListItem` a bullet, and every other category a plain paragraph.

### Strengths

- Typed elements make the intermediate result easy to inspect or process differently downstream.
- Automatic partitioning provides a broad-format entry point.
- The local Markdown mapping is short, explicit, and easy to adjust.

### Tradeoffs

- The lightweight adapter discards most element metadata and does not preserve all layout or hierarchy available from Unstructured.
- Categories outside the three special cases are flattened to plain paragraphs, so complex structures can lose fidelity.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-unstructured\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\unstructured_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/` and calls `partition(filename=...)` separately for each one.
- It converts the returned elements with `elements_to_markdown()` and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `unstructured_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Marker 1.10.2

### Conversion approach

Marker uses a model-backed, PDF-oriented `PdfConverter`. The repository creates the converter from `create_model_dict()`, renders each source, and extracts the Markdown string with `text_from_rendered()`.

### Strengths

- Targets structured Markdown recovery from PDFs, including layout-heavy content.
- Uses a single rendered result from which the repository directly extracts Markdown.
- Can benefit substantially from CUDA acceleration on complex documents.

### Tradeoffs

- It is the most PDF-specific path; unsupported source formats fail per file.
- Model loading and conversion are computationally heavy, particularly with CPU-only PyTorch.
- The default configuration can retain running headers, produce broken image references or mojibake, and encounter worker or deeply nested rendering failures on difficult PDFs.

### Repository flow

- Run `& .\.venv-marker\Scripts\python.exe .\codes\marker_test.py` from the repository root.
- The script recursively sorts files under `source/`, initializes one `PdfConverter` with default Marker 1.10.2 configuration, and processes files sequentially.
- For each file it calls the converter, takes the first value returned by `text_from_rendered()`, and writes the same relative path with a `.md` suffix under `marker_results/`.
- Per-file exceptions are reported while the batch continues; any failure makes the final process exit with status 1.

## Choosing a loader

- Choose Docling when a structured document model and direct Markdown export are the best fit.
- Choose Unstructured when typed elements and a customizable local mapping are more useful than high-fidelity Markdown serialization.
- Choose Marker when PDF-focused, model-backed structure recovery justifies the greater compute cost and narrower input support.

All three runners overwrite an existing output for the same source-relative path. They are comparison scripts rather than a shared production ingestion pipeline, and generated Markdown should be evaluated for reading order, headings, lists, tables, equations, images, and metadata instead of by file size alone.

  <script>
    (() => {
      "use strict";

      const source = document.getElementById("markdown-source").textContent;
      const target = document.getElementById("document");

      const escapeHtml = (value) => value
        .replaceAll("&", "&amp;")
        .replaceAll("<", "&lt;")
        .replaceAll(">", "&gt;")
        .replaceAll('"', "&quot;")
        .replaceAll("'", "&#39;");

      const renderInline = (value) => {
        const code = [];
        let html = value.replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, (_, contents) => {
          code.push(`<code>${escapeHtml(contents)}</code>`);
          return `\u0000CODE${code.length - 1}\u0000`;
        });

        html = escapeHtml(html).replace(
          /\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)/g,
          (_, label, href) => {
            const safeHref = /^(https?:\/\/|\.\.?\/|#)/.test(href) ? href : "#";
            return `<a href="${escapeHtml(safeHref)}">${label}</a>`;
          }
        );

        return html.replace(/\u0000CODE(\d+)\u0000/g, (_, index) => code[Number(index)]);
      };

      const renderMarkdown = (markdown) => {
        const lines = markdown.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n").split("\n");
        const output = [];
        let paragraph = [];
        let inList = false;

        const closeParagraph = () => {
          if (paragraph.length) output.push(`<p>${renderInline(paragraph.join(" "))}</p>`);
          paragraph = [];
        };
        const closeList = () => {
          if (inList) output.push("</ul>");
          inList = false;
        };

        for (const line of lines) {
          const heading = /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/.exec(line);
          const item = /^-\s+(.+)$/.exec(line);

          if (heading) {
            closeParagraph();
            closeList();
            const level = heading[1].length;
            output.push(`<h${level}>${renderInline(heading[2])}</h${level}>`);
          } else if (item) {
            closeParagraph();
            if (!inList) {
              output.push("<ul>");
              inList = true;
            }
            output.push(`<li>${renderInline(item[1])}</li>`);
          } else if (!line.trim()) {
            closeParagraph();
            closeList();
          } else {
            closeList();
            paragraph.push(line.trim());
          }
        }

        closeParagraph();
        closeList();
        return output.join("\n");
      };

      try {
        target.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(source);
      } catch (error) {
        target.innerHTML = '<p id="render-error">The embedded document could not be rendered.</p>';
        console.error(error);
      }
    })();
  </script>

from pathlib import Path

from docling.backend.pypdfium2_backend import PyPdfiumDocumentBackend
from docling.datamodel.base_models import InputFormat
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter, PdfFormatOption


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SOURCE_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "source"
OUTPUT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "docling_results"


def output_path_for(source_path: Path) -> Path:
    relative_path = source_path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)
    return (OUTPUT_DIR / relative_path).with_suffix(".md")


def main() -> None:
    source_files = sorted(
        path for path in SOURCE_DIR.rglob("*") if path.is_file()
    )

    if not source_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"No source files found in: {SOURCE_DIR}")

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    converter = DocumentConverter(
        format_options={
            InputFormat.PDF: PdfFormatOption(
                backend=PyPdfiumDocumentBackend
            )
        }
    )

    print(f"Found {len(source_files)} source file(s).")

    converted = 0
    failures = []

    for source_path in source_files:
        output_path = output_path_for(source_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        print(f"Converting: {source_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")

        try:
            result = converter.convert(source_path)

            markdown = result.document.export_to_markdown()
            output_path.write_text(markdown, encoding="utf-8")

            converted += 1
            print(f"Markdown written to: {output_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")

        except Exception as error:
            failures.append((source_path, error))
            print(f"FAILED: {source_path.name}: {error}")

    print(f"Docling complete: {converted} converted, {len(failures)} failed.")

    if failures:
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---UNSTRUCTURED---

from pathlib import Path

from unstructured.partition.auto import partition


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SOURCE_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "source"
OUTPUT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "unstructured_results"


def elements_to_markdown(elements) -> str:
    lines = []
    for element in elements:
        category = element.category
        text = str(element)
        if category == "Title":
            lines.append(f"# {text}")
        elif category == "Header":
            lines.append(f"## {text}")
        elif category == "ListItem":
            lines.append(f"- {text}")
        else:
            lines.append(text)
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


def output_path_for(source_path: Path) -> Path:
    relative_path = source_path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)
    return (OUTPUT_DIR / relative_path).with_suffix(".md")


def main() -> None:
    source_files = sorted(path for path in SOURCE_DIR.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
    if not source_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"No source files found in: {SOURCE_DIR}")

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    print(f"Found {len(source_files)} source file(s) for Unstructured.")

    converted = 0
    failures: list[tuple[Path, Exception]] = []

    for source_path in source_files:
        output_path = output_path_for(source_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        print(f"Converting: {source_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")

        try:
            elements = partition(filename=str(source_path))
            output_path.write_text(elements_to_markdown(elements), encoding="utf-8")
            converted += 1
            print(f"Markdown written to: {output_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")
        except Exception as error:
            failures.append((source_path, error))
            print(f"FAILED: {source_path.name}: {error}")

    print(f"Unstructured complete: {converted} converted, {len(failures)} failed.")
    if failures:
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from pathlib import Path

from marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter
from marker.models import create_model_dict
from marker.output import text_from_rendered


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SOURCE_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "source"
OUTPUT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "marker_results"


def output_path_for(source_path: Path) -> Path:
    relative_path = source_path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)
    return (OUTPUT_DIR / relative_path).with_suffix(".md")


def main() -> None:
    source_files = sorted(path for path in SOURCE_DIR.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
    if not source_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"No source files found in: {SOURCE_DIR}")

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    converter = PdfConverter(artifact_dict=create_model_dict())
    print(f"Marker converter initialized. Found {len(source_files)} source file(s).")

    converted = 0
    failures: list[tuple[Path, Exception]] = []

    for source_path in source_files:
        output_path = output_path_for(source_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        print(f"Converting: {source_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")

        try:
            rendered = converter(str(source_path))
            markdown_output, _, _ = text_from_rendered(rendered)
            output_path.write_text(markdown_output, encoding="utf-8")
            converted += 1
            print(f"Markdown written to: {output_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")
        except Exception as error:
            failures.append((source_path, error))
            print(f"FAILED: {source_path.name}: {error}")

    print(f"Marker complete: {converted} converted, {len(failures)} failed.")
    if failures:
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

 output_path_for(source_path: Path) -> Path:
    relative_path = source_path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)
    return (OUTPUT_DIR / relative_path).with_suffix(".md")


def main() -> None:
    source_files = sorted(path for path in SOURCE_DIR.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
    if not source_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"No source files found in: {SOURCE_DIR}")

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    converter = PdfConverter(artifact_dict=create_model_dict())
    print(f"Marker converter initialized. Found {len(source_files)} source file(s).")

    converted = 0
    failures: list[tuple[Path, Exception]] = []

    for source_path in source_files:
        output_path = output_path_for(source_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        print(f"Converting: {source_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")

        try:
            rendered = converter(str(source_path))
            markdown_output, _, _ = text_from_rendered(rendered)
            output_path.write_text(markdown_output, encoding="utf-8")
            converted += 1
            print(f"Markdown written to: {output_path.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)}")
        except Exception as error:
            failures.append((source_path, error))
            print(f"FAILED: {source_path.name}: {error}")

    print(f"Marker complete: {converted} converted, {len(failures)} failed.")
    if failures:
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### understanding
This Python comparison project converts documents to Markdown using three independent loaders: Docling, Unstructured, and Marker. The goal adds a concise Markdown overview of those loaders plus a static HTML page that opens in Chrome and displays the overview’s content.

### requirements
- Create one concise Markdown document covering Docling, Unstructured, and Marker.
- For each loader, explain its processing approach, output behavior, and notable project-specific strengths or limitations.
- Keep technical claims consistent with the existing implementations and README: Docling exports a structured document model, Unstructured maps partitioned elements through a lightweight local adapter, and Marker uses a model-backed PDF converter.
- Create an HTML file intended for Chrome that presents the Markdown document’s content.
- Preserve headings, lists, links, code spans, and tables when the Markdown is rendered rather than displayed as plain text.
- Use UTF-8 and provide a clear readable layout.
- Keep the solution simple and avoid altering the existing loader or chunking workflows.

### constraints
- The repository has no JavaScript package manifest, frontend framework, web server, or build pipeline, so the viewer should be static and require no project build step unless a new runtime requirement is explicitly chosen.
- The project targets Windows and PowerShell, with Chrome named as the browser.
- Chrome generally prevents a `file://` HTML page from fetching a sibling Markdown file, so direct double-click support requires embedding the Markdown, using a user-selected file, or another workaround; fetching the file normally requires serving the directory over HTTP.
- Existing loader details and versions are documented in `README.md`: Docling 2.113.0, Unstructured 0.24.1, and Marker 1.10.2.
- The three loaders run independently and use separate result directories and Python environments; the new files must not imply a shared loader runtime that does not exist.

# Context

_Gathered 2026-08-08 11:22:22Z by the requirements agent._

## Goal

Create a simple markdown document explaining the three document loaders discussed and then write a html file that can show this markdown file's content in chrome browser

## Understanding

Create a concise Markdown guide describing the project’s Docling, Unstructured, and Marker document loaders, along with a static HTML viewer that renders the guide as formatted content. The HTML must work in Chrome when opened directly from the filesystem, without a server, build step, or additional user interaction.

## Requirements

# Deliverables

- Add one concise Markdown document covering Docling, Unstructured, and Marker.
- Add one standalone HTML file that displays the Markdown document’s content as rendered, formatted HTML.

# Markdown content

- Explain each loader’s processing approach, output behavior, and important project-specific strengths or limitations.
- Keep claims aligned with the existing project implementation and README:
  - Docling exports from a structured document model.
  - Unstructured partitions documents into elements and maps them through the project’s lightweight local adapter.
  - Marker uses a model-backed PDF converter.
- Do not suggest that the three loaders share a runtime; they operate independently with separate environments and result directories.
- Keep the document simple, clear, and readable.

# HTML viewer

- Render the guide as formatted text, not raw Markdown source.
- Preserve the document’s headings, lists, links, inline code, and tables.
- Work when the HTML file is double-clicked or opened directly in Chrome using a `file://` URL.
- Require no local HTTP server, frontend build process, browser extension, file picker, or command-line setup.
- Avoid runtime fetching of the sibling Markdown file because Chrome may block local-file requests.
- Include or embed everything needed to display the guide within the HTML file while retaining the Markdown file as the canonical documentation deliverable.
- Use UTF-8 and a clean, readable layout suitable for desktop Chrome.

# Scope

- Do not modify existing loader, conversion, chunking, environment, or result-directory behavior.
- Do not add a frontend framework, JavaScript package setup, or project build pipeline.

## Constraints from the existing codebase

- The repository has no existing JavaScript package manifest, frontend framework, web server, or browser build pipeline.
- Direct `file://` operation rules out relying on `fetch()` to load the sibling Markdown file.
- Any rendering logic or rendered content required at viewing time must therefore be self-contained in the HTML file.
- The project targets Windows and PowerShell, and Chrome is the required viewing environment.
- Existing documented versions are Docling 2.113.0, Unstructured 0.24.1, and Marker 1.10.2; version claims should remain consistent with the repository.
- The three loaders use independent Python environments and separate result directories.

## Open risks

- Because direct-file Chrome viewing prevents reliable loading of the Markdown file, a self-contained HTML copy can drift from the canonical Markdown document if either is edited later. The implementation should minimize this duplication or clearly establish a simple regeneration/update mechanism without adding a runtime dependency.
- If the HTML uses an externally hosted Markdown-rendering library, offline viewing will fail and future CDN changes may break the page; embedding rendered HTML or local rendering code is safer for the double-click requirement.

## Clarifications

**Q.** Should the HTML render the Markdown as formatted content, or display the raw Markdown source text?

**A.** Render as formatted text

**Q.** Must the HTML work when opened directly by double-clicking it (`file://`), or may the project directory be served through a local HTTP server so the page can fetch the Markdown file?

**A.** a simple double-clicking the HTML file or opening it with chrome to view is fine

## The requirements this is all in service of

# Context

_Gathered 2026-08-09 08:49:19Z by the requirements agent._

## Goal

Build a normal responsive website in this empty target repository.

Make it a clean static website for a small local service called 'Bhai Digital Studio'. It should have a homepage, basic navigation, an about/services section, a small portfolio/gallery section, and a contact section. Use simple, maintainable HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Keep the site easy to open locally in a browser without requiring a backend.

Make the implementation complete enough that a reviewer can inspect the files, open the site, and see a polished working website.

## Understanding

This repository is essentially empty: it only contains a minimal README and no package manifests or source files. The goal is to create a complete static, locally openable responsive website for a small local service named Bhai Digital Studio, using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript without a backend or build step.

## Requirements

## Functional Requirements
- Create a static website for `Bhai Digital Studio`.
- Include a homepage with clear brand identity and basic navigation.
- Include an about/services section describing the studio and its core services.
- Include a small portfolio/gallery section showing example work or representative project tiles.
- Include a contact section with practical contact details or a simple static contact form UI.
- Navigation should work within the page or across static sections/pages.
- The site must be responsive across desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
- The site should be polished enough for a reviewer to open locally and inspect visually.

## Technical Requirements
- Use simple, maintainable HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Keep the implementation static and backend-free.
- Make the site easy to open locally in a browser, preferably via an `index.html` entry point.
- Organize assets and scripts clearly, with no unnecessary framework or build tooling.
- JavaScript should be limited to small progressive enhancements such as mobile navigation, gallery interaction, or form feedback.

## Constraints from the existing codebase

- The repository has no existing app structure, framework, source files, package manifest, or build system to integrate with.
- The solution should therefore be plain static files rather than a Node, React, or backend project.
- The current README contains only the repository name and imposes no product or design constraints.
- Because no real business copy, images, phone number, address, or portfolio assets exist in the repo, implementation should use tasteful placeholder content unless specific real content is provided later.

## How to decide

Approve when the wave's tasks are implemented in a way that works and is consistent with the requirements. Minor style differences are not grounds for rework.

Send it back for rework when something is actually wrong: a task not implemented, implemented incorrectly, obviously broken, contradicting the requirements, or contradicting an explicit user choice.

Scope your judgement to THIS wave. Later waves have not run yet, so work they are responsible for being absent is not a defect — do not send a wave back for failing to do something that was never its job.

Be specific. "The error handling could be better" cannot be acted on. "`health.py` returns 200 when the database ping raises, at line 24" can.

- Frontend must use vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (no frameworks like React, Vue, etc.)
- Express server must listen on port **27107** specifically (non-standard port)

- Database name must be `temp_work_db` with `contacts` and `testimonials` collections
- Existing HTML/CSS/JS files from T-001 should be refined/extended, not discarded
- Frontend must remain fully functional even if backend server is not running (graceful degradation)
- Contact form error handling must display error message and allow retry (not silent fallback)
- Testimonials must be fetched from MongoDB via API, not hardcoded in HTML
- Test must be runnable with `npm test` without external services
- File structure must enable parallel editing (separate files to minimize merge conflicts)
- Contact form fields (name, email, message) already defined in HTML; validation must handle these
- Mobile-responsive layout already defined; enhancements must maintain responsive behavior
- Smooth scrolling already implemented in CSS; additional JS enhancements must complement existing behavior

## Open risks

- Port 27107 is non-standard and may conflict with other services; planner should verify this choice doesn't conflict in the user's environment
- Testimonials section requires both API endpoint and MongoDB collection to be created and wired together; if these tasks run in parallel, they must be synchronized in integration phase
- Contact form error/retry flow adds complexity to frontend JS; must handle both successful submission, API errors, and unreachable backend gracefully
- Testimonials endpoint must be tested to ensure it returns data in format expected by frontend display logic
- MongoDB `testimonials` collection requires seed data or initialization logic; unclear if this should be manual setup or automated in test/seed script

- Database name must be `temp_work_db` with `contacts` and `testimonials` collections

## Open risks

- Port 27107 is non-standard and may conflict with other services; planner should verify this choice doesn't conflict in the user's environment
- Testimonials section requires both API endpoint and MongoDB collection to be created and wired together; if these tasks run in parallel, they must be synchronized in integration phase
- Contact form error/retry flow adds complexity to frontend JS; must handle both successful submission, API errors, and unreachable backend gracefully

- Port 27107 is non-standard and may conflict with other services; planner should verify this choice doesn't conflict in the user's environment
- Testimonials section requires both API endpoint and MongoDB collection to be created and wired together; if these tasks run in parallel, they must be synchronized in integration phase
- Contact form error/retry flow adds complexity to frontend JS; must handle both successful submission, API errors, and unreachable backend gracefully
- Testimonials endpoint must be tested to ensure it returns data in format expected by frontend display logic
- MongoDB `testimonials` collection requires seed data or initialization logic; unclear if this should be manual setup or automated in test/seed script

## Clarifications

**Q.** What port should the Express server listen on? (Goal does not specify; this could be 3000, 5000, 8000, or another port and would configure server.js)

**A.** 27107

**Q.** Should the testimonials section display static hardcoded HTML content, or should testimonial data be stored in MongoDB and fetched via an API endpoint?

**A.** for now, create and store hypothetical data in the mongoDB and use that

**Q.** When the backend API is unreachable, should the contact form display an error message to the user and allow retry, or fall back to displaying a static thank-you message as it currently does in the static version?

**A.** error message and the retry

- JavaScript enhancements: mobile navigation toggle, smooth scrolling, active section highlighting, portfolio filtering by category, contact form validation, testimonial async loading with fallback, form submission to backend API
- Graceful degradation when backend server is unavailable

## Backend
- Local Node.js Express server on port 27107
- MongoDB connection to `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017` database `temp_work_db`
- POST `/api/contact` endpoint: accepts name/email/message, validates, stores in `contacts` collection, returns JSON response
- GET `/api/health` endpoint: verifies server and MongoDB connectivity
- GET `/api/testimonials` endpoint: returns testimonials from `testimonials` collection with fallback seeding
- CORS handling for local requests
- Error handling with clear JSON error responses

## Testing
- Automated tests verifiable with `npm test` or `node <script>`
- Must verify: server starts, MongoDB connection works, `temp_work_db` is used, contacts can be inserted and retrieved

Implement GET /api/health returning JSON that confirms server status, MongoDB reachability, and database name; POST /api/contact with validation and normalized insert fields; GET /api/testimonials with seeded or fallback testimonials; CORS for local file/browser development; clear JSON error responses; and exported start/stop or app/server helpers needed by tests. package.json should include start and test scripts but not own the test implementation. In final JSON report, state artifact visibility for context.md, learnings.md, and user_choices.md, and append the required PARALLEL_ARTIFACT_TEST marker to learnings.md only if workflow permissions allow append-only artifact writes.

- Opening `index.html` directly shows complete polished website
- Running local server enables contact form submission to MongoDB

- Results reviewable through filesystem evidence, test output, and MongoDB/API behavior

## Constraints from the existing codebase

- Must use vanilla HTML, CSS, JavaScript (no frameworks)
- Must use local MongoDB only (no cloud database)
- Must use Express for backend (lightweight)
- Server runs on port 27107
- Database must be named `temp_work_db` at `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017`
- POST `/api/contact` endpoint for contact form submission
- GET `/api/health` endpoint for connectivity check
- Contact submissions stored in `contacts` collection
- Tests use same production `temp_work_db` database with ability to flush contents
- Test data persists for manual verification
- Tests use separate setup script for initialization
- Frontend must work as file:// protocol (no backend) and with backend on localhost:27107
- File structure: `index.html`, `assets/css/styles.css` (or `styles.css`), `assets/js/main.js` (or `app.js`), `server.js`, `db/connection.js`, `db/schema.js`, `package.json`, `tests/api.test.js`, `README.md`
- Parallel first-wave tasks must edit distinct files to avoid conflicts
- Incremental, evidence-based implementation for resume capability

## Goal, as the user stated it
Test run for this target repository. Build a small pricing tool for 'Bhai Digital Studio'.

Foundational work: implement the actual pricing/discount calculation logic as a small, dependency-free JavaScript module (pricing.js), including realistic edge cases — tiered volume discounts, a minimum order threshold, currency rounding rules, and rejection of invalid inputs. Separately, implement an input-validation module (validation.js) that checks a raw order object against the required shape before it reaches the pricing module — malformed input, missing fields, out-of-range quantities. These two modules do not depend on each other, but nothing else in this project can be built until both exist and are correct. This is the part that needs real care and judgment, not boilerplate — get the edge cases right.

Once pricing.js and validation.js exist, build three small, nearly identical static preview pages, each wiring the pricing module up against a different fixed product (product-a.html, product-b.html, product-c.html): product details, a couple of sample orders run through the pricing module, and the computed totals shown on the page. These three pages are mechanical and repetitive — same structure, different static data — and none of them can be written until the pricing and validation modules exist, since they import and call them directly.

Every coding agent must, immediately after starting, read this run's shared learnings.md in full using the exact mechanism described in your brief, and note whether it found any earlier entries before doing anything else. ## Your earlier survey
### understanding
Bhai Digital Studio currently has a portfolio website with Express/MongoDB backend. The goal is to build a new pricing calculator tool as a foundational module set: two dependency-free JavaScript modules (pricing.js and validation.js) implementing core business logic, followed by three identical static product preview pages that wire these modules together with fixed sample data.

### requirements
## Functional Requirements

1. **pricing.js module**
   - Calculate total cost for an order based on unit price and quantity
   - Apply tiered volume discounts (e.g., different discount percentages at different order thresholds)
   - Enforce a minimum order threshold (reject orders below it)
   - Apply currency rounding rules for final totals
   - Reject invalid inputs (negative quantities, null/undefined prices, etc.)
   - Export a single function that takes an order object and returns pricing result
   - Zero external dependencies

2. **validation.js module**
   - Validate that raw order input matches required shape before pricing
   - Check all required fields are present
   - Check field types (e.g., quantity is a number, not a string)
   - Check quantities are within valid ranges (positive, not NaN, not Infinity)
   - Detect and reject malformed input
   - Export validation errors clearly
   - Zero external dependencies
   - Does not depend on pricing.js

3. **Three static product preview pages**
   - product-a.html, product-b.html, product-c.html
   - Each displays product details (name, description, unit price)
   - Each runs 2-3 sample orders through the pricing module
   - Each displays computed order totals on the page
   - Each imports pricing.js and validation.js directly (no bundler)
   - Minimal styling, focused on functionality

## Technical Constraints

- pricing.js and validation.js must be pure JavaScript with zero npm dependencies
- Static HTML pages must load modules via `<script>` tags (no module bundler)
- No test framework required; validate logic manually or via simple sanity-check scripts
- Keep files small and focused (not production code)
- Both validation.js and pricing.js must exist and pass before product pages are written
- Each agent must read learnings.md in full before starting and append own entry after finishing

### constraints
- Repository is currently set up for a portfolio website with Express/MongoDB backend; pricing tool is a separate, independent feature using only static HTML/JS
- Must maintain existing portfolio site files; pricing tool is additive
- No backend required; pricing logic must be client-side only
- No database; all product/order data is hard-coded on the HTML pages

## The user's answers
- Q: What currency should the pricing tool use (USD, GBP, EUR, PKR, etc.), and what rounding precision (standard 2 decimal places?)?
  A: USD and the standard round off
- Q: What are the specific tiered discount rules? (e.g., 0-9 units: no discount, 10-19 units: 10% discount, 20+ units: 15% discount?)
  A: 0-9 units: no discount, 10-19 units: 10% discount, 20+ units: 15% discount
- Q: What is the minimum order threshold value (e.g., minimum 5 units, or minimum $50 total)?
  A: minimum 3 units
- Q: What are the product details for product-a, product-b, and product-c? (name, description, unit price for each)
  A: use hypthetical data
- Q: What is the exact structure of an order object that validation.js must check? (e.g., {productId, quantity, unitPrice} or different fields?)
  A: productId, quantity, unitPrice

## Your earlier survey
### understanding
Bhai Digital Studio is a web design/branding agency. The goal is to build a standalone pricing tool—a small, vanilla JavaScript application with no backend or database. The tool will include reusable calculation modules (pricing and validation) wired into three nearly identical static HTML preview pages, each demonstrating pricing against a different fixed product.

### requirements
## Functional Requirements

- **pricing.js module** - Dependency-free JavaScript module that:
  - Accepts a valid order object and returns a pricing result (total, line items, discount applied)
  - Implements tiered volume discounts (e.g., different discount percentages at different quantity thresholds)
  - Enforces a minimum order threshold (rejects orders below it)
  - Rounds currency values according to a defined precision rule
  - Rejects invalid inputs with a clear error message
  - Handles realistic edge cases (partial quantity discounts, discount boundaries, rounding edge cases)
  - Exports a single calculation function

- **validation.js module** - Input validation module that:
  - Accepts a raw, unvalidated order object
  - Validates required fields are present and correctly typed
  - Validates field values are in-range and well-formed (e.g., quantities > 0)
  - Returns structured validation result (ok: boolean, errors: object)
  - Does NOT depend on pricing.js; can be used independently
  - Rejects malformed input (missing fields, wrong types, out-of-range values)

- **Three static HTML preview pages** (product-a.html, product-b.html, product-c.html):
  - Identical HTML structure and styling across all three
  - Display a product name, description, unit price, and any relevant metadata
  - Import and use both validation.js and pricing.js
  - Show 2–3 hard-coded sample orders, each validated and priced
  - Display computed totals, discount amounts, and final prices on the page
  - Minimal styling (reuse or extend existing style.css)

## Technical Requirements

- All JavaScript modules are vanilla ES5+ with no external dependencies
- pricing.js and validation.js must be synchronous, testable units
- HTML pages must be static (no DOM manipulation beyond rendering sample results)
- Use standard module patterns (IIFE or ES module syntax as appropriate)
- Keep all files small and focused (single responsibility)
- No backend, no database, no test framework (minimal manual verification acceptable)
- Learnings.md file: Read at start, append one entry at end documenting what was implemented and confirming both read and write succeeded

## Data & Domain Constraints

- The pricing tool must be realistic for a design/branding agency (e.g., pricing tiers might reflect package complexity or delivery time)
- Currency formatting must handle common precision edge cases (e.g., rounding $9.995 to $10.00 vs $9.99)
- Discount application must be transparent (show base price, discount amount, and final price)

### constraints
- Repository already has vanilla JavaScript with IIFE patterns and ES5+ syntax (see assets/js/main.js); follow this style
- CSS is minimal and semantic (style.css is ~37 lines); any new styling should match this simplicity
- No existing build tool, bundler, or test framework in use; all three HTML files must load modules via `<script>` tags
- Project uses no Node.js runtime dependencies for frontend code (package.json has only Express and MongoDB, neither needed here)
- Git repository is active; any new work should be in small, focused commits
- learnings.md does not yet exist; must be created as part of first agent's work
